Hilbert's tenth problem and his broader programme asked for a mechanical procedure that could decide any mathematical statement. Turing's 1936 paper defined what a mechanical procedure is in order to show that no such procedure exists — the machine was invented to answer Hilbert, and then turned out to be useful.
Everything a program can prove is inside Turing's definition of the computable. Logic Theorist was the first program to go looking for theorems inside that fence, twenty years after it was drawn.
